IS ,6540. 1972

Indian Standard
CODE FOR HYGIENIC CONDITIONS FOR MANUFACTURE AND HANDLING OF ICE FOR HUMAN CONSUMPTION

o. r 0

REW0 RD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Tnstitution on 28 April 1972, after the draft finalized by the Food Hygiene, Sampling- and Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council.

0.2 Ice is widely consumed in foods, drinks and in various other forms, specially during summer season. In the course of its manufacture, transport, storage, handling and distribution, ice is open to microbial contamination from a variety of sources including the water freezing equipment, containers and persons engaged in its manufacture,
0.3 Ice is sold to the consumers through a large variety of channels. Once ice, has been formed, the temperature and the conditions on the surface are normally inhibitory to microbial multiplication. Ice may get contaminated on surface by organic matter, it may come in contact with, due to faulty handling, It is, therefore, imperative that ice is washed thoroughly in clean potable running water before consumption.

0.4 Unless the manufacture, transport, storage and handling of ice is governed by strict hygienic code in respect of layout, plant and personnel, the quality of ice cannot he considered as safe for human consumption. It is essential that on melting, the ice should give a water of potable quality in its bacteriological, physical and chemical features, 'These factors have been considered in the preparation of this code.
0.5 This code is subject to the provisions of the Factories Act, 1948; and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, and the Rules framed thereunder as amended from time to time.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This code specifies the hygienic conditions required for the manufacture, transport, storage and handling of ice for human consumption.

3

IS .6540�1912

2. MANUFACTURE
2.1 Ice Plaat or Factory
2.1.1 Sitl and Premises

2.1.1.1 The building in which ice is manufactured shall be preferably situated in open, clean and healthy surroundings far away from roadside where lot of dust arises due to vehicular traffic; Jltarbage dnmps; cattle sheds: open sewage drains or other places likely to breed flies. Premises should not have objectionable odour 01� smoke. There shall be no accumulation of trash, garbage or similar waste in the vicinity of the plant.
2.1.1.2 The structure of the building shall be of permanent nature and shall be suitable in size, construction and design to facilitate maintenance and hygienic operations. It should provide sufficient space for housing of equipment as is necessary for hygienic operations.. The material of construction shall be brick, plaster, cement, concrete, tile or any other equivalent material which ensures cleanliness.

2.1.1.3 N0lortion of the building shall be used for domestic purposes unless separate by suitable partitions or locations or other effective means so as to avoid contamination of the products with undesirable micro-organisms, odour, chemicals, filth or other foreign material. 2.1.1.4 Separate rooms of sufficient size should be provided for manufacture and storage of ice, washing and sterilization of containers and utensils; and storage of raw materials and other requisites.

2.1.1.5 The floors of the rooms should be constructed of concrete or other equally impervious and easily cleanable material. They should be smooth, suitably sloped for drainage of water and provided with trapped drains. 2.1.1.6 \Van~ and ceilings of the rooms should have a smooth, non-ausorbent light coloured surfaces free from crevices and angles to facilitate their efficient cleaning. 1'hey shall be painted or Iime-washed and cleaned as often as necessary. The junction of the Boor with the walls and the junction between the two walls should be rounded to prevent accumulation of dust.
2.1.1.7 The manufacturing unit shall be adequately lighted and ventilated keeping in view the number of workers. their hours of work and nature of operation. Ventilation and lighting shall also be in accordance with the Factories Act, 1948. as amended from time to time. Propel' ventilation is essential to prevent condensation and drlppage. Exhau:lt fans shall be provided where necessary,
4

IS r 6540.1972

2.1.1.8 The manufacturing room shall be made fly proof, rodent proof and bird proof and should be provided with self-closing double doors. The doors and windows should be covered with fly-proof wire-gauze, and they should open outwards.
2.1.1.9 The rooms and the area surrounding the factory building should be kept clean and dust-free. 2.1.1.10 The building shall be maintained in proper state of repair and cleanliness at all times. 2.2 GeDeral Factory HYlieDe

2.2.1 Rubbish shall be collected in covered receptacles and shall not be allowed to scatter on the floor of the factory. Suitable facilities for the collection and removal of refuse, floor sweepings and dirt in covered containers and for disposal of wastes should he provided. It should be disposed of in a manner which is not detrimental to the hygiene of the
surroundings of the disposal.
2.2.2 Adequate measures shall be taken to prevent mould growth on equipment and internal surfaces of processing and storage rooms. Adequate steps shall be taken to prevent infestation bv cockroaches and other household pests.

2.2.3 When pesticides are used, care shall he exercised to prevent contamination of equipment, and other materials. Under no circumstances shall these be used during processing.

2.2.4 Floors and drains shall be kept clean. In the manufacturing room, drain shall be provided with detachable covers.
2.2.5 On no account shall the manufacturing room be used or oonverted to a store room. 2.2.6 No lavatory, sink, cesspool, 01� garbage shall be so situated or maintained that odours or fumes therefrom pervade any room where the ice is prepared or stored. 2.2.7 Proper places shall be provided for storage of buckets and other cleaning gear.

brushes,

2.2.1 The factorv effluents shall not be le-t off on roads or in open, outside the factory � premises.

2.2.10 There shall be no cobwebs in any part of the unit. domestic animals shall not be allowed in any part of the unit.

2.3 EquiplDeDt aDd Container CleaDliae��
2.3.1 Installation and Construction of Equipment - The equipment should be constructed and installed in such a manner as to facilitate efficient cleaning and sanitization and easy dismantling and assembling of all the parts that come in contact with water or ice. All the equipment, containers, lids and pipes shall he smooth, impervious and corrosion resistant. All the materials used for construct ion of those surfaces which come into contact ' . .�ith ice shall be non toxic.

2.3.2 r:lttlfling and Sanitiration - All the containers and lids should be cleaned thoroughly with the use of sodium carbonate or sodium bicarbonate or any other suitable detergent solution and sanitized with 50 ppm chlorine solution prior to their use. The residual chlorine may be removed by flushing the (ll]U iprnent with water to be used for manufacture of ice.
2.4 Water Supply - Water is the only ingredient used in ice manufacture and maximum carp should be taken with regard to its quality both chemical and mirrobiological.

2.4.1 For qualitv tolerances for water used for manufacture of IS: 3957..1966� should be n-ferred to as guideline.

ice~

2.4.1.1 There shall be an adequate supply of safe and potable water, 2.4.2 The water prior to storage should be prechlorinated between 0'2 to O'5 ppm of residual chlorine. 2.4.3 The storage tanks for water should, unless completely sealed, be kept covered with tight-titting lids. examined daily and cleaned properly and sanitized by spraying 100 ppm chlorine solution at least once every month. The date of the last cleaning and next cleaning shall be prominently displayed 011 the storage tanks. 2.4.4 \Vater sample shall be got examined period ically . chemically and bacteriolog-ically as desired by the licensing authority. A record of such examination shall be maintained. 2.4.5 Running water under pressure shall be eaaily accessible to all rooms and areas in which ice is manufactured and equipment are washed. 2.4.5.1 Hot and cold water in ample supply shall be provided for plant clean-up needs.

2.5 El11ployee Hygiene
2.5.1 Every person employed for manufacture of ice in the .factory shall be medically examined by an authorized registered medical practitioner and the examination shall include X-Ray of the chest for tuberculosis.
�(~ua1ity

tolerance for water fOJ' ice Inanufactlu'e.

6

IS ,6540.1972
The examination shall also include: examination of stool for protozoal and helminthic infestation for those parasites which are transmitted by ingestion, and for the presence of Salmonella, ShigelltZ species and Vibrio chollrae; urine; and blood examination for venereal diseases. Subsequently, the employee shall be medically examined once a year or more frequently, if 'necessary, to ensure that he is medically fit and free from communicable diseases. A record of such examination shall be maintained .
. 2.5.1.1 It shall be impressed on all employees that they should notify the medical officer and management, cases of fever, vomiting, diarrhoea, typhoid, dysentry, boils, cuts and sores and ulcers ( however small), discharging ears and notifiable diseases occurring in their own homes and families.

2.5.1.2 No worker who is suspected to be suffering from any of the disorders listed in 2.5.1.1 shall be permitted to work inside the plant. The supervisor shall check the personal hygiene of the workers before " the start of work and whenever they enter any processing room after any absence.

2.5.2 Employees shall keep their finger nails short and clean and wash their hands with soap or detergent and water before commencing work and after each absence, specially after using sanitary conveniences. Towels used for drying hands should be clean. _ No worker should allow his hands or any part of his body or clothing to come into contact with the water which goes in the manufacture of ice. He should adopt strict hygienic practices so as to avoid adding any microbial contamination to the water or ice. 2.5.3 All employees shall be inoculated and vaccinated against the enteric groups of diseases once a year and against smallpox Once in two years. In case of an epidemic all workers shall be inoculated. A record shall be kept.
2.5.4 No worker shall be allowed to work without proper clothing and footwear. 2.5.5 Employees shall be provided with clean uniforms (preferably white) or aprons or both and clean washable caps, where necessary. 2.5.5.1 Separate room or place for changing the clothes shall be provided. The clothes shall not be hung in any pr~cessing room.

2.5.5.2 The uniforms shall not be worn outside the plant but put on just before starting the work and changed when leaving.
2.5.6 Eating, spitting, nose cleaning or the use of tobacco in any form or chewing betel leaves shall be prohibited within the manufacturing area of the unit. Notice to this-effect shall be prominently displayed and enforced,

7

IS 16540 .1972

2.5.7 Sufficient and suitable sanitary conveniences shall be provided, maintained and kept clean in every factory. The conveniences shall be properly lighted. Separate conveniences shall he provided for each sex. The conveniences should have self closing doors which shall not open directly into any work room in the factory. The conveniences shall always be maintained clean and in good repairs. 2.5.8 Sufficient number of wash basins with adequate provision of nail brushes, soap and towels, latrines and urinals in the prescribed manner should be provided, conveniently situated and accessible to workers at all times while they are at the factory (see also Table 3 of IS : 1172-1971 *). The wash basins should be installed in or alongside the sanitary conveniences, �
2.6 Q,aality of Ice 2.6.1 Ice shall be got examined periodically, chemically and bacteriologically. A record of such examination shall be kept. 2.6.2 Ice not meant for human consumption should be suitably coloured.

3. TRANSPORT, STORAGE AND HANDLING 3.1 Ice sellers shall procure ice only from approved licensed sources. 3.2 All persons handling ice should be healthy and free from communicable diseases. They should keep their finger nails short and clean, wear clean clothes and observe strict hygienic practices.

3.3 All vehicles used for transportation of ice should be so constructed and operated as to give reasonable protection to their contents from access of flies, dust and other contaminate. The vehicles should be duly licensed by the local health authority and should be maintained clean.
3.4 All premises where ice is stored or sold should be fully licensed for the purpose by the local health authority. The premises should be maintained clean and should be so constructed as to provide reasonable protection to ice from access of flies, dust and other contaminants. 3.5 Ice should be stored either in clean insulated metal containers or wrapped/covered in clean hessian on impervious clean floors. 3.6 Ice from selling points should be got examined periodically, chemically and bacteriologically. A record of such examination shall be maintained.

3.7 When ice is served in common cold drinks, the ice shall be thoroughly washed in clean potable running water before insertion. If the ice i. required to be crushed before use, it shall be beaten in clean cloth.
